content.text: Suggest as part of implemnting this a full test is done with the "LITE" APIs disabled - to catch any "internal" use of the LITE APIs.  Testing should also include demo objects, particularly those that use content models, to ensure there's no internal usages buried there.  Also testing that a "permanently moved" response is handled sensibly if existing content models use the REST URLs - we don't want to break anyone's existing content models with this release.
Need to ensure that the new REST API contains everything that the LITE APIs did - see

Moving to 3.5.  Now documented as deprecated, but we have some work to go before removing (or at least providing a "moved permanently" respose for a release or two).  Some tests still use LITE APIs, and probably some server code also.
It's not just tests that still use the /get/ endpoint, some of the demo objects do, and some of the core Fedora code does also.
Deprecate the LITE REST APIs - deprecate in next release by using 301 - Moved Permanently responses, then remove completely in a future release.
This will support having a single dereferencable URI for a Fedora resource which can then be used as the definitive resource identifier.
